title: Vasquez: private faith of the promise, with hope of pardon, is needed for justification
source_text: XXXIX. Quibus consentanea sunt quae leguntur apud Vasquezium in 1.2. Tom. 2. disp. 200. cap. 4. Ubi diserte docet ad justificationem tum primam, tum secundam, non tantum conducere, sed necessarium esse, non solum fidem Catholicam dogmatum, historiae & promissionum, quae universe factae sunt; sed etiam fidem privatam promissionis, qua quisque credat sibi Deum non defuturum, neque negaturum auxilium efficax, & se tandem a Deo justificandum. Nam, inquit, si aliquis existimaret Deum sibi negaturum auxilium efficax ad salutem, omnis ad justificationem progressus & dispositio impediretur, ut manifeste constat. Inter reliqua enim necessaria ad justificationem primam debet esse spes veniae; haec autem sine fide peculiari esse non potest. Nam quamvis aliquis crederet ea quae universis promissa sunt, nempe, vere poenitentibus peccata remitti, & poenitentia aliisque operibus bonis a Deo obtineri veniam & justificationem: tamen, nisi etiam credat se iis operibus quae exercet a Deo veniam consecuturum, quae sane est fides peculiaris promissionis, non poterit hanc veniam sibi a Deo sperare, ac proinde neque justificationis compos erit, siquidem spes non minus necessaria est dispositio ad justificationem quam fides.
pass_a_gloss: To which those things are agreeable which are read in Vasquez in 1.2. Tom. 2. disp. 200. cap. 4. Where he expressly teaches that for justification, both first and second, it not only helps but is necessary not only Catholic faith of dogmas, history, and promises which have been made universally, but also a private faith of the promise by which each one believes that God will not fail him, nor deny efficacious help, and that he finally is to be justified by God. For, he says, if someone should think that God would deny him efficacious help unto salvation, every progress and disposition toward justification would be hindered, as is manifestly clear. For among the remaining things necessary for first justification there ought to be hope of pardon; but this cannot be without a peculiar faith. For although someone should believe those things which are promised to all, namely that to the truly penitent sins are remitted, and that by repentance and other good works pardon and justification are obtained from God: nevertheless, unless he also believes that by those works which he exercises he will obtain pardon from God, which indeed is a peculiar faith of the promise, he will not be able to hope for this pardon for himself from God, and consequently will not be a partaker of justification, since hope is no less a necessary disposition to justification than faith.
pass_b_english: Vasquez requires more than catholic assent to general promises.
A private faith that God will not fail me—and hope of pardon—belongs to the disposition for justification.

choices.why: Vasquez’s non-catholic faith of the promise.
